meta.disclaimer: Equalaw provides legal information and guided next steps, not legal advice. For binding advice, consult a qualified legal specialist or your nearest District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), which provides free legal aid to eligible citizens.

domains.label: Consumer dispute (defective product / service / e-commerce)
domains.rights_summary: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 protects you against defective goods, deficient services, unfair trade practices, and misleading ads. You can seek refund, replacement, compensation, and removal of unfair practices.

authority.name: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
authority.escalation: State Commission (claims over Rs. 1 crore) and National Commission (over Rs. 10 crore)

domains.limitation: File within 2 years from the date the cause of action arises.
documents: Invoice / order confirmation / receipt
Warranty card if any
Screenshots of listing, chat, and payment
Written complaint already sent to the seller and their reply (if any)
Photos/video of the defect
domains.template_hint: A complaint to the District Consumer Commission stating parties, facts, defect/deficiency, relief sought (refund/replacement/compensation), and a verification clause.

domains.label: Cheque bounce / money recovery
domains.rights_summary: Under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, a bounced cheque is a criminal offence. You must first send a written demand notice; if unpaid within 15 days, you can file a criminal complaint. For informal loans, a civil recovery suit is the route.

authority.name: Judicial Magistrate First Class (for S.138) / Civil Court (for recovery suit)
authority.online_portal: https://njdg.ecourts.gov.in (case status); filing is done at the local court
authority.helpline: Contact your nearest District Legal Services Authority for help drafting and filing

domains.limitation: Send the demand notice within 30 days of the cheque return memo. File the complaint within 30 days after the 15-day payment window expires.
documents: The dishonoured cheque
Bank return memo ('cheque return' slip)
Proof of the underlying debt (loan agreement, messages, invoices)
Copy of the demand notice and postal receipt / acknowledgement
domains.template_hint: A statutory demand notice under S.138 NI Act demanding payment of the cheque amount within 15 days, sent by registered post.

domains.label: Cybercrime / online fraud
domains.rights_summary: Cyber fraud and online offences are covered by the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. For financial fraud, reporting within the 'golden hour' greatly increases the chance of freezing and recovering funds.

authority.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal / local Cyber Crime Police Station
authority.helpline: Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 (report financial fraud immediately)

domains.limitation: Report financial fraud immediately — ideally within 1 hour ('golden hour'). No fixed limitation to file, but act fast.
documents: Transaction IDs, UPI/bank references, and amounts
Screenshots of the fraudulent messages, calls, or profiles
Bank statement showing the debit
Your ID proof
Any phone numbers / URLs / account numbers of the fraudster
domains.template_hint: A cybercrime complaint capturing the timeline, the fraudulent transactions/accounts, and a request to freeze accounts and investigate.

domains.label: Workplace: unpaid wages / wrongful termination
domains.rights_summary: Workers are protected by the Payment of Wages Act, the Industrial Disputes Act, and the new Labour Codes. You are entitled to timely wages, lawful termination procedure, notice/retrenchment compensation, and a safe workplace.

authority.name: Office of the Labour Commissioner (state) / Labour Court
authority.online_portal: https://shramsuvidha.gov.in (and your state labour department portal)
authority.helpline: Contact your State Labour Department; DLSA can help you file

domains.limitation: Wage claims: generally within 12 months. Industrial disputes: raise promptly; delays weaken the claim.
documents: Appointment letter / employment contract
Salary slips and bank statements
Termination or resignation letter
Any emails / messages about the dispute
Attendance or work records
domains.template_hint: A complaint to the Labour Commissioner stating employment details, the wages/termination grievance, and the relief sought.

domains.label: Domestic violence / women's protection
domains.rights_summary: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 gives the right to protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, and custody orders. Cruelty and dowry harassment are also criminal offences. Help is free and confidential.

authority.name: Protection Officer (district) / Magistrate's Court
authority.online_portal: Approach the District Protection Officer or a registered Service Provider / One Stop Centre
authority.helpline: Women Helpline 181 · Police 112 · One Stop Centre (Sakhi)

domains.limitation: No strict limitation for seeking protection — you can apply at any time. Act as soon as it is safe to do so.
documents: Any medical records of injuries
Photos, messages, or recordings evidencing abuse
Details of income/assets (for maintenance)
ID and address proof
Names and details of witnesses if any
domains.template_hint: A Domestic Incident Report / application under the PWDV Act seeking protection, residence, and monetary relief. Handle with sensitivity and a safety-first tone.

domains.label: Landlord / tenant dispute
domains.rights_summary: Tenancies are governed by your State Rent Control / Tenancy Act and the rent agreement. Tenants cannot be evicted without due process, and security deposits must be refunded per the agreement.

authority.name: Rent Authority / Rent Controller (as per your state's Rent Act)
authority.online_portal: Check your state's Rent Authority portal (e.g., Model Tenancy Act states)
authority.helpline: DLSA can guide you on your state's procedure

domains.limitation: Money claims (e.g., deposit): generally within 3 years. Act promptly.
documents: Registered rent agreement / lease
Rent payment receipts or bank records
Proof of the security deposit paid
Written communication with the landlord
Photos of the property condition
domains.template_hint: A demand notice to the landlord/tenant demanding refund of deposit / cure of the breach within a reasonable time before approaching the Rent Authority.

domains.label: Right to Information (getting records from a public office)
domains.rights_summary: The Right to Information Act, 2005 lets any citizen ask for information held by a public authority. The Public Information Officer (PIO) must respond within 30 days (48 hours if it concerns life or liberty).

authority.name: Public Information Officer (PIO) of the concerned department
authority.escalation: First Appellate Authority, then the State / Central Information Commission
authority.online_portal: https://rtionline.gov.in (for central bodies); states have their own portals
authority.helpline: DLSA and many NGOs help draft RTI applications free

domains.limitation: PIO must reply in 30 days. First appeal: within 30 days of the reply/deadline. Second appeal: within 90 days.
documents: Clear list of the information you want
The name of the department / office
Rs. 10 application fee (waived for Below Poverty Line applicants)
Your address for the reply
domains.template_hint: An RTI application addressed to the PIO listing specific, answerable questions and citing the applicant's fee status.

domains.label: Free legal aid eligibility & how to apply
domains.rights_summary: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, free legal aid — including a free lawyer, court fees, and drafting — is a right for eligible people: women, children, SC/ST, persons with disabilities, trafficking/disaster victims, industrial workmen, persons in custody, and anyone with an annual income below the state's prescribed limit.

authority.name: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), located in every district court complex
authority.online_portal: https://nalsa.gov.in (apply online via the NALSA portal or at the DLSA front office)

domains.limitation: No limitation — you can apply at any time, before or during a case.
documents: Proof of identity (Aadhaar / voter ID)
Income certificate or ration card (to show eligibility)
Caste certificate / disability certificate if claiming that ground
Brief written summary of your legal problem
Any documents related to your case
domains.template_hint: An application to the District Legal Services Authority stating the applicant's eligibility ground, a summary of the legal problem, and a request for free legal aid / a panel legal specialist.
